$description: #270 when-research — PROPOSED `when` predicates, s253-D1 shape (gate half + prose half). NOTHING ENACTED. No meta, schema, rules index, runbook or gate was touched by this lane.
$shape: s253-D1: gate half = machine-checkable clause; prose half = beats/yields sentence naming the sibling and quoting its roles.json when.

$confidence_scale.canon: a predicate already adopted in our own repo — the work is a copy, not an invention
$confidence_scale.consensus-external: 3+ public systems state the same KIND of criterion
$confidence_scale.single-external: one system states it, or the systems conflict on the cut
$confidence_scale.none: no source found; the predicate is proposed from our own meta prose or is a declared guess

proposals.when_gate: selection = single AND options.count <= 5 AND every option is visible without opening anything AND effect = on-submit
proposals.when_prose: the default single-answer control of the input role; beats dropdown (roles.json when: null — proposed "6–15 options and the column cannot spare the height") below six options because every option stays in view and costs no click; yields to segmented-control (proposed "the choice re-presents content already on screen") when the answer changes a view rather than a form value, and to combobox (proposed "options >= 16, closed list") when the list outgrows the page.
disagreements: THE NUMBER. radio→dropdown cut point: Polaris 4 · M3 5 · Ant 5 · Spectrum 6 · USWDS 7 · GOV.UK + NN/g + Atlassian give NO number and prefer radios always. The KIND of criterion is unanimous; the cut is arbitrary.
proposals.daves_call: pick one number for the radio→dropdown cut, or rule that we carry no number and use "fits without scrolling" instead.

proposals.when_gate: selection = multiple OR (selection = binary AND effect = on-submit) AND the group needs a legend
proposals.when_prose: the default multi-answer control; beats radio (proposed "selection = single") whenever zero, one or several answers are all valid, and beats switch (proposed "effect = immediate") whenever a Save or Continue must be pressed before anything happens; a lone checkbox is the right control for one on/off answer inside a form (terms, marketing consent).
disagreements: none found — seven systems agree on cardinality AND on deferred effect
proposals.daves_call: nothing. This one is free. Ratify as written.

proposals.when_gate: selection = binary AND options.count = 2 AND effect = IMMEDIATE (no Save, no Submit, no confirm step) AND validation = none
proposals.when_prose: beats checkbox (proposed "effect = on-submit") on exactly one test — does the world change the instant the thumb moves; yields to checkbox whenever the setting is part of a form that is submitted, whenever more than one option can be on, or whenever the field can be in error, because a switch has no error state; yields to segmented-control when the two options are opposed alternatives rather than on and off.
disagreements: none on the immediacy test — 5 of 5 systems state it. Spectrum ADDS a consequence nobody else names: a switch cannot show an error.
proposals.daves_call: adopt immediacy as the discriminator, and say whether Spectrum's no-error-state consequence becomes a HARD rule here (it would make switch illegal in any validated form).

proposals.when_gate: selection = single AND options.count in 2..5 AND the choice RE-PRESENTS content already on screen (view, scale, range, period) AND labels are one or two words AND destination = same
proposals.when_prose: beats radio (proposed "selection = single, <= 5 options, effect on submit") when the answer is not a form value but a presentation switch applied at once; beats tabs because tabs move between destinations and this stays in place (our own meta, verbatim); yields to switch when the two options are on and off rather than two presentations, and to dropdown when the label set will not fit one track.
disagreements: the COUNT ceiling: Carbon and M3 give none; ours is proposed from the track-width constraint, not from a source. Nobody outside names a maximum.
proposals.daves_call: the count ceiling (5 proposed), and whether "applied at once" is required — if it is, a segmented control inside a submitted form becomes illegal.

proposals.when_gate: selection = single AND options.count in 6..15 AND the options are familiar enough to recognise on sight AND vertical space is constrained
proposals.when_prose: the compact single-answer field; beats radio (proposed "<= 5 options") only once the visible list would cost more height than the page can spare; yields to combobox (proposed "options >= 16") when the list outgrows scrolling, to multi-select when the answer is a set, and to account-selector (proposed "the option IS an account") in any payment journey.
sources: USWDS select (the only explicit 7–15 range found)
disagreements: THE DEEPEST DISAGREEMENT ON THE PAGE. USWDS 7–15. Polaris 4+. Carbon not-below-3. GOV.UK: "last resort", cites research that users find selects difficult. NN/g: prefer radios. Two systems actively discourage the component our canon treats as the default form field.
proposals.daves_call: whether a dropdown is our DEFAULT single-select field or our LAST RESORT. Every number below follows from that one word.

proposals.when_gate: selection = single AND options.count >= 16 AND options come from a CLOSED list (free text is never committed) AND the user can name what they want before they see it
proposals.when_prose: beats dropdown (proposed "6–15 options") when typing beats scrolling — countries, payees, currencies, branches (our own meta, verbatim); yields to dropdown when the set is short and browsable (our own antiPattern), and to tags-input when a value NOT in the list may be committed, which is a different contract, not a wider one.
disagreements: the NUMBER again: USWDS 15, Spectrum 6, Carbon none. A 9-option list is a combobox at Adobe and a plain select at USWDS.
proposals.daves_call: the dropdown→combobox cut (16 proposed, from USWDS). Same decision as the radio cut — rule them together or not at all.

proposals.when_gate: selection = multiple AND options.count >= 10 AND the chosen values must stay VISIBLE after the list closes AND the list stays open between choices
proposals.when_prose: beats a checkbox group (proposed "selection = multiple") only when the option set is too long to show as checkboxes and the running answer must be readable as a row of chips; yields to a checkbox group whenever all the options fit on the page, because checkboxes need no disclosure; yields to the count-summary variant rather than truncating the chip row (our own antiPattern).
sources: USWDS select ("Users often don’t understand how to choose multiple items")
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE. Not one of the nine systems distinguishes a chip multi-select from a checkbox group. They all say "use checkboxes". Our threshold of 10 has NO source — it is a guess dressed as a number and is marked as such.
proposals.daves_call: everything. This predicate has no external support at all. Either rule the boundary yourself or leave multi-select with no `when` and say so out loud.

proposals.when_gate: selection = single AND the option IS an account (name · masked number · balance) AND the journey = payment / transfer / standing order
proposals.when_prose: beats dropdown and combobox in every payment journey because the option carries three fields and a balance the reader must compare before choosing — our meta forbids a raw <select> for the same choice; yields to the masked account chip once the choice is made and the row becomes a receipt.
disagreements: no external analogue exists — this is a domain component. Silence here is expected, not a gap.
proposals.daves_call: confirm the journey list is the right fence (payment / transfer / standing order), or widen it.

proposals.when_gate: records >= 2 AND fields-per-record >= 3 AND the reading is COMPARISON ACROSS records on the same fields AND interaction = none
proposals.when_prose: the default of the record-list role (roles.json when: "default, read-mostly"); beats list-items (roles.json when: "<= 3 fields per item, tappable") whenever the reader must compare the same field down a column; yields to data-grid (roles.json when: "sort / filter / select / edit-in-place is required") the moment any interaction is needed, and is never used for layout (our own antiPattern).
disagreements: none — our adopted canon and GOV.UK say the same thing in different words
proposals.daves_call: only whether to COPY the adopted roles.json predicate onto the meta. The criterion itself is already yours.

proposals.when_gate: records >= 2 AND fields-per-record >= 3 AND (sort OR filter OR row-selection OR edit-in-place) is required
proposals.when_prose: beats table (roles.json when: "default, read-mostly") exactly when an interaction is required — the 2026-06-22 rubric decision A our meta already quotes: they are distinct components; yields to table whenever the screen only reads, because a grid carries an ARIA grid contract and a tab-stop model that a read-only page should not pay for.
sources: Carbon structured-list ("If multiple row selection is needed, use a data table instead")
disagreements: none — Carbon reaches the identical split from the other side
proposals.daves_call: only the copy onto the meta. Same as table.

proposals.when_gate: records >= 2 AND fields-per-record <= 3 AND each row is TAPPABLE (the row is a destination or an action) AND no field is compared down a column
proposals.when_prose: beats table (roles.json when: "default, read-mostly") when the row is a thing to open rather than a row to compare — roles.json when: "<= 3 fields per item, tappable"; yields to table when a fourth field appears or a column must be read down, and to data-grid when rows must be selected in bulk (Carbon reaches the same line).
sources: GOV.UK summary-list ("Do not use it for tabular data")
disagreements: the number 3 is OURS ALONE. Carbon says "simple data", GOV.UK says "not tabular data"; nobody outside counts fields. Our 3 is already adopted, so it is a ruled number, not a sourced one — worth knowing the difference.
proposals.daves_call: whether "tappable" is REQUIRED (it excludes a static bulleted list, which this same meta also covers — a real ambiguity in the component's scope).
